Chavacano

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Spanish tragedia.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /tɾaˈxedja/, [t̪ɾaˈxe.d͡ʒa]
  • Hyphenation: tra‧ge‧dia

Noun

[edit]

tragedia

  1. tragedy

Esperanto

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From tragedio +‎ -a.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /traɡeˈdia/
  • Rhymes: -ia
  • Syllabification: tra‧ge‧di‧a

Adjective

[edit]

tragedia (accusative singular tragedian, plural tragediaj, accusative plural tragediajn)

  1. tragic

Further reading

[edit]
  • “tragedia”, in Plena Ilustrita Vortaro de Esperanto [Complete Illustrated Dictionary of Esperanto], 2020, →ISBN
  • “tragedia”, in Reta Vortaro [Online Dictionary] (in Esperanto), 1997-present

Finnish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Latin tragoedia, from Ancient Greek τραγῳδία (tragōidía).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈtrɑɡediɑ/, [ˈt̪rɑ̝ɡe̞ˌdiɑ̝]
  • Rhymes: -iɑ
  • Syllabification(key): tra‧ge‧di‧a
  • Hyphenation(key): tra‧ge‧dia

Noun

[edit]

tragedia

  1. tragedy
    Synonym: murhenäytelmä

Italian

[edit]
Italian Wikipedia has an article on:
tragedia
Wikipedia it

Etymology

[edit]

From Latin tragoedia, from Ancient Greek τρᾰγῳδῐ́ᾱ (trăgōidĭ́ā), from τρᾰ́γος (trắgos, “male goat”) + ᾠδή (ōidḗ, “song”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /traˈd͡ʒɛ.dja/[1][2]
    • Rhymes: -ɛdja
    • Hyphenation: tra‧gè‧dia
  • IPA(key): (careful style, Old Italian) /tra.d͡ʒeˈdi.a/[1][2]
    • Rhymes: -ia
    • Hyphenation: tra‧ge‧dì‧a

Noun

[edit]

tragedia f (plural tragedie)

  1. tragedy
    Antonym: commedia

Related terms

[edit]
  • trageda
  • tragediografo
  • tragico
  • tragicommedia

See also

[edit]
  • comedia

References

[edit]
  1. ↑ 1.0 1.1 tragedia in Bruno Migliorini et al., Dizionario d'ortografia e di pronunzia, Rai Eri, 2025
  2. ↑ 2.0 2.1 tragedia in Luciano Canepari, Dizionario di Pronuncia Italiana (DiPI)

Anagrams

[edit]
  • gradiate

Polish

[edit]
Polish Wikipedia has an article on:
tragedia
Wikipedia pl

Etymology

[edit]

Learned borrowing from Latin tragoedia.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /traˈɡɛ.dja/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɛdja
  • Syllabification: tra‧ge‧dia

Noun

[edit]

tragedia f (related adjective tragiczny)

  1. tragedy

Declension

[edit]
Declension of tragedia
singular plural
nominative tragedia tragedie
genitive tragedii tragedii/tragedyj (archaic)
dative tragedii tragediom
accusative tragedię tragedie
instrumental tragedią tragediami
locative tragedii tragediach
vocative tragedio tragedie

Further reading

[edit]
  • tragedia in Wielki słownik języka polskiego, Instytut Języka Polskiego PAN
  • tragedia in Polish dictionaries at PWN

Portuguese

[edit]

Etymology 1

[edit]

Verb

[edit]

tragedia

  1. inflection of tragediar:
    1. third-person singular present indicative
    2. second-person singular imperative

Etymology 2

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

tragedia f (plural tragedias)

  1. pre-reform spelling (used until 1943 in Brazil and 1911 in Portugal) of tragédia
    • 1880, Maria Amalia Vaz de Carvalho, “A proposito de um livro [Apropos a book]”, in Contos e phantasias [Short stories and fantasies]‎[2], 2nd edition, Lisbon: Parceria Antonio Maria Pereira, published 1905, page 241:
      E quem terá forças para conservar-se espectador indifferente d’essa dolorosa tragedia de que é theatro o mundo inteiro!
      And who shall have the strength to remain an indifferent witness to this painful tragedy for which the whole world is the theater!

Spanish

[edit]
Spanish Wikipedia has an article on:
tragedia
Wikipedia es

Etymology

[edit]

From Latin tragoedia, from Ancient Greek τρᾰγῳδῐ́ᾱ (trăgōidĭ́ā), from τρᾰ́γος (trắgos, “male goat”) + ᾠδή (ōidḗ, “song”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /tɾaˈxedja/ [t̪ɾaˈxe.ð̞ja]
  • Audio (Colombia):(file)
  • Rhymes: -edja
  • Syllabification: tra‧ge‧dia

Noun

[edit]

tragedia f (plural tragedias)

  1. tragedy, catastrophe
  2. (drama) a tragedy play
    Antonym: comedia
  3. sob story

Related terms

[edit]
  • trágico
  • tragicomedia

Further reading

[edit]
  • “tragedia”, in Diccionario de la lengua española [Dictionary of the Spanish Language] (in Spanish), online version 23.8.1, Royal Spanish Academy [Spanish: Real Academia Española], 15 December 2025
